summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with altered mental status and groin pain, found to be due to a urinary tract infection caused by pan-sensitive Pseudomonas aeruginosa, likely exacerbated by a missed indwelling catheter change. He was treated with intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam initially, then transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin after culture results. His mental status improved, consistent with resolution of metabolic encephalopathy. A right-sided varicocele was identified on scrotal ultrasound but deemed non-urgent with no evidence of mass effect on imaging. Left ankle erythema resolved and was attributed to bruising rather than cellulitis, leading to discontinuation of vancomycin. Hyperkalemia on admission normalized without intervention. He was discharged to extended care on a 12-day course of ciprofloxacin, with instructions to continue skin care and follow up with urology for his stable renal mass.
